correctness.rationale: Each of the 36 ordered pairs must be partitioned by six balls of at most six descendants. All six codewords therefore have maximal balls and a unique diagonal, forcing form a b c a. Their twelve bidirectional spoke edges and three twice-oriented single edges form a three-edge complement. A complete five-graph-type case split forces this complement to be a perfect matching. Cross-edge uniqueness then forces a directed 3-cycle among matched pairs. There are 15 matchings, 2 cycles, 8 orientation assignments; internal label swaps flip exactly two bits, yielding two parity orbits of 120, exchanged by reversal. Standalone exact-cover enumeration and all 720 alphabet relabelings independently reproduce the 240 and two 120 counts. The proof does not extrapolate an experiment.

value.rationale: The complete set of extremizers for an exceptional small-alphabet perfect deletion design is a natural finite classification. The new 240-count and two parity-distinguished orbits expose structural information not carried by size-spectrum theorems; they give an explicit symmetry-sensitive reproducibility benchmark, not an arbitrary unmotivated numeric slice.
